title: Grammar: Hypothetical Structures — Supposing, Imagine, What if
grammarTip:
"Supposing", "Imagine", "What if" — гипотетические ситуации:

SUPPOSING / IMAGINE → предположим что... (+ Past Simple для нереального):
"Supposing you had a million dollars — what would you do?"
"Imagine you could fly — where would you go?"

WHAT IF → что если бы... (риторический вопрос о гипотетическом):
"What if we missed the train? What would happen?"
"What if she hadn't come? Everything would be different."

💡 Все три конструкции работают как 2nd или 3rd Conditional — используй was/were, would, had.

rows.example: Supposing you had a million dollars — what would you do?

rows.form: Supposing + past perfect → would have + pp
rows.example: Supposing she had known — would she have acted differently?

rows.form: "Supposing" can replace "If" entirely in hypothetical sentences
rows.example: Supposing it rained tomorrow — would you still come?
What if we changed the plan entirely?
What if she hadn't sent that email?

rows.form: "What if" often appears as a standalone question
rows.example: What if everything we know is wrong?

grammarExtra.title: As if / As though: Comparison to Unreal

rows.form: Verb + as if/as though + past simple
rows.example: He acts as if he owned the place. (He doesn't.)

rows.form: Verb + as if/as though + past perfect
rows.example: She looked as though she had seen a ghost.

rows.form: Note: After "as if/though," was OR were is acceptable
rows.example: He looks as if he was/were exhausted.

rows.form: Had + subject + past participle (= If + subject + had + pp)
rows.example: Had she arrived earlier, she would have caught the train.

rows.form: Were + subject + to + infinitive (= If + subject + were to)
rows.example: Were we to accept, the consequences would be significant.

rows.form: Should + subject + infinitive (= If + subject + should)
rows.example: Should you require further information, please contact us.

rows.form: Imagine + what if inside one sentence
rows.example: "Imagine what might have happened if they had stayed."
"Suppose we agreed — it would feel as though we had given up."

rows.form: These combinations appear in academic debate and creative writing
rows.example: "What if, supposing the theory is correct, we reconsidered our approach?"

exercises.text: "Supposing you ___ (find) a wallet full of money — what would you do?"
"What if they ___ (not/arrive) on time? The whole plan would have collapsed." (past hypothetical)
exercises.hint: What if + past perfect for past hypotheticals

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form for "as if."
exercises.text: "She talks ___ she knew everything about the subject."
exercises.hint: As if + past simple = unreal present comparison

exercises.text: "If you should need help, call us immediately." → ___ you need help, call us immediately.
"___ you won the lottery — would you quit your job?" (speculative question)
exercises.hint: All three can introduce this type of hypothetical

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct inverted form.
exercises.text: "___ she to refuse the offer, the company would seek other partners." (= If she were to refuse)
exercises.hint: Were + subject + to-infinitive = formal inverted present conditional

exercises.text: "He acted as though he had never met her before."
opts: He had genuinely never met her
He behaved as if he didn't know her, even though he did
He introduced himself for the first time
exercises.correct: He behaved as if he didn't know her, even though he did
exercises.hint: "As though + past perfect" = comparison to an unreal/contrary past situation

exercises.text: "___ they had invested earlier, the returns would have been much higher." (= If they had invested)
exercises.hint: Inverted past conditional: Had + subject + pp

opts: What if you will change your mind?
What if you changed your mind?
What if you are changing your mind?
What if you change to your mind?
exercises.correct: What if you changed your mind?
exercises.hint: What if + past simple for hypothetical

exercises.instruction: Complete with "as if" or "as though" + past perfect.
exercises.text: "She looked ___ she had just run a marathon." (She looked exhausted)
exercises.hint: As if/though + past perfect for unreal past comparison

exercises.instruction: Which is the formal inverted version of "If you should have any questions…"?
exercises.hint: Should + subject = inverted conditional for polite offers/conditions

exercises.text: "___ you could redesign this city — what would you change first?"
"Supposing she ___ the truth — what would have happened?"
"He spent money ___ it ___ no limit." (= As if there were no limit)
exercises.hint: As if + past simple/were for unreal present comparison

opts: If they had reviewed the contract, the problem would not have occurred.
If only they had reviewed the contract.
Had they reviewed the contract, the problem would not have occurred.
Supposing they had reviewed the contract — the problem would not have occurred.
exercises.correct: Had they reviewed the contract, the problem would not have occurred.

exercises.instruction: What is the difference between these two?
exercises.text: "What if we tried a new approach?" vs "What if we had tried a new approach?"
exercises.hint: Past simple = present/future hypothetical; past perfect = past hypothetical

questions.text: "Supposing you ___ the job — would you take it?" (future hypothetical)
"___ they had acted sooner, the crisis would have been avoided." (Formal inverted — past)
questions.hint: Had + subject + pp = inverted past conditional

questions.text: "She acts as though she ___ the whole city." (She doesn't own it)
questions.hint: As if/though + past simple = unreal present

questions.text: "___ you require assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us." (Formal inverted polite condition)
Which introduces a past hypothetical correctly?
opts: What if she had decided to leave
questions.correct: What if she had decided to leave
questions.hint: Past perfect after "what if" = past hypothetical

questions.text: "Were we to accept the terms, the consequences would be serious." This is a formal present hypothetical.
questions.hint: Were + subject + to-infinitive = formal present conditional

questions.text: "He looked as though he ___ up all night." (He had been up all night)
questions.hint: As though + past perfect = unreal past comparison

questions.text: "___ you could redesign the education system — where would you start?"
Which is NOT a correct hypothetical starter?
"What if we ___ the whole strategy?" (Present/future hypothetical — rethink)
questions.hint: What if + past simple = present/future hypothetical

questions.text: "___ she to submit the proposal today, the board would consider it this week." (= If she were to submit)
questions.hint: Were + subject + to-infinitive = formal present conditional
